items.label: f10-nested-create
items.front: How does createApplication write an application and its applicants?
items.back: One nested Prisma create inside an interactive transaction: loanApplication.create connects createdBy to the session user, connects assignedOfficer only when a LOAN_OFFICER creates it, and creates the PRIMARY party plus an optional CO_APPLICANT through parties.create. An APPLICATION_CREATED audit row follows in the same transaction, and the record comes back with the detail include for the presenter.

items.label: f05-query-client-freshness
items.front: How is the browser's QueryClient created, and what keeps its data fresh?
items.back: One QueryClient per tab, made in a useState initializer so re-renders keep the same cache. Its defaults are staleTime 15 s and refetchOnWindowFocus off, and no query sets a polling interval. So nothing pushes or polls another user's change into an open page: the tab sees it only after a refetch that its own activity triggers.

items.label: f02-sequence-guard
items.front: How does the provider-event sequence guard work, and where does it fall short?
items.back: Each verification keeps a providerSequence high-water mark. An event below it is stored with appliedToWorkflow false and receivedOutOfOrder true; an equal or higher one overwrites the verification. Gaps: equal sequences re-apply, there is no row lock, no idempotency key, and the "provider" is a logged-in loan officer.

items.label: f07-presenter-boundary
items.front: What does the presenter layer do, and how are its input types tied to the queries?
items.back: It turns Prisma records into JSON-safe view shapes: Decimal amounts to strings, Dates to ISO strings, and an explicit field list per view, so a new column does not reach the browser by accident. Its input types are Prisma.LoanApplicationGetPayload over typeof applicationSummaryInclude and applicationDetailInclude, so editing an include changes the presenter's type and tsc flags any field that disappeared.

items.label: f08-command-transaction-scope
items.front: Take createCondition. What runs before its transaction, and what runs inside it?
items.back: Before: the visibility lookup on the shared client. Inside one interactive transaction: insert the OPEN condition, write the CONDITION_CREATED audit row, then reconcileAndPersistStage, which re-reads the aggregate on the transaction client, recomputes and persists the stage, and loads the full detail for the response. Fact, audit and stage commit together or not at all.

items.label: f03-two-gates
items.front: In what order does createRouteHandler process a request?
items.back: Resolve the session; 401 if none and the route is not allowAnonymous; assert the declared permission (403); run the handler; in the catch, ZodError becomes 400, AppError keeps its status, anything else is logged and returned as 500.

items.label: f04-guards-outside-tx
items.front: Why is it a problem that recordDecision and disburseApplication run their guards before prisma.$transaction?
items.back: The guard reads state outside the transaction, so a concurrent write can change the facts between the check and the update. The transaction makes the writes atomic, but not the decision to allow them; there is no optimistic locking on stateVersion.

items.label: f09-detail-payload-growth
items.front: What does applicationDetailInclude load, and why does its cost grow with a file's age?
items.back: Every party, verification and condition, plus every transition, external event (with its JSON payload) and audit row, each with no take. History tables only grow, and every workflow command loads this include inside its write transaction via loadApplicationDetailById, so response size and in-transaction read time rise with each action. A paged history endpoint, or a take on the history relations, would cap it.

items.label: f01-rule-order
items.back: 1 declined or deniedAt: DENIED; 2 servicingHandedOffAt: SERVICING_HANDOFF; 3 disbursedAt: DISBURSEMENT; 4 no intake: INTAKE; 5 any FAILED or missing/non-PASSED required verification: VERIFICATION; 6 decision PENDING or REFER: CREDIT_DECISIONING; 7 a FAILED condition: CONDITIONS; 8 an OPEN condition: CONDITIONS; 9 APPROVED: APPROVED; else unchanged. The order is the policy.

items.label: f06-prisma-client-singleton
items.front: Why does prisma.ts keep the client and its pg Pool on globalThis outside production?
items.back: next dev re-evaluates modules on hot reload; a fresh PrismaClient per reload would open a new pool each time and leak connections. So the module reuses globalThis.prisma and globalThis.prismaPool when present, and stores them only when NODE_ENV is not production. Prisma 7 talks to Postgres through the @prisma/adapter-pg driver adapter wrapping that one pg Pool.

items.prompt: CREDIT_PULL is PASSED at providerSequence 5. A second event also carrying providerSequence 5 arrives with status FAILED. What happens?

choices.text: It is stored as out of order and not applied
It is applied, and the verification becomes FAILED
It is ignored, as sequence 5 was already seen
It is refused as a duplicate by a unique index

choices: It is stored as out of order and not applied
It is applied, and the verification becomes FAILED
It is ignored, as sequence 5 was already seen
It is refused as a duplicate by a unique index

items.explanation: The guard is >=, so an equal sequence counts as fresh: the event is applied and overwrites PASSED with FAILED. isOutOfOrder uses <, so it is not flagged either.

items.prompt: A developer adds a required number field, termMonths, to createApplicationSchema and changes nothing else. What does that change do?

choices.text: tsc passes, and each create from the form now gets a 400
tsc passes, and the API stores termMonths as null for now
tsc fails in the service, whose input type lacks the field
tsc fails in the form, which is typed from the zod schema

choices: tsc passes, and each create from the form now gets a 400
tsc passes, and the API stores termMonths as null for now
tsc fails in the service, whose input type lacks the field
tsc fails in the form, which is typed from the zod schema

items.explanation: The route parses into the schema's inferred type and passes it on (route.ts:27-28), but the service's input type is written out by hand (application-command-service.ts:152-173). Passing an object with an extra property where a narrower type is expected is legal TypeScript (excess-property checks apply only to object literals), and the client's CreateApplicationInput is a third hand-written copy (use-applications.ts:36-54). A probe with zod 4.3.6 and TypeScript 5.9.3 compiled that shape with exit 0. At runtime the form's body has no termMonths, so parse throws a ZodError and the wrapper answers 400 Validation failed. The service would ignore the field anyway, and there is no column to store it.

items.prompt: An operator changes a signed-in user's role from LOAN_OFFICER to SERVICING_AGENT directly in the database. The user's cookie is untouched. When do the API routes start applying the new role?

choices.text: On the user's next request, as each one reloads the user row
At the next login, as the signed cookie carries the old role
Once the browser's session query refetches the new role
Never, as the cookie's HMAC no longer matches the new role

choices: On the user's next request, as each one reloads the user row
At the next login, as the signed cookie carries the old role
Once the browser's session query refetches the new role
Never, as the cookie's HMAC no longer matches the new role

items.explanation: The cookie value is the user id plus an HMAC of that id (session.ts:27-30); the role is not in it. getSessionFromRequest verifies the signature, then loads the user by id and builds the session's role from that row (session.ts:67-79), and createRouteHandler resolves the session on every request (route-handler.ts:71-73). So the very next API call is authorized with SERVICING_AGENT's permissions and visibility. The signature covers only the id, so a role change cannot break it, and the browser's session query only affects what the UI displays, not what the server enforces.

items.prompt: A proxy in front of the app answers a detail-page mutation with 502 and an HTML error page. What error does the mutation end up holding?

choices.text: An ApiClientError with status 502 and Request failed.
An ApiClientError whose message is the HTML page text
No error, as apiFetch reads a non-JSON body as empty
A SyntaxError from parsing the HTML, with the 502 lost

choices: An ApiClientError with status 502 and Request failed.
An ApiClientError whose message is the HTML page text
No error, as apiFetch reads a non-JSON body as empty
A SyntaxError from parsing the HTML, with the 502 lost

items.explanation: apiFetch awaits response.json() on line 27 before it checks response.ok on line 29. Parsing an HTML body rejects with a SyntaxError (probe on Node 22.16's fetch Response, which follows the Fetch standard like browsers do), so the ApiClientError branch on lines 29-31 never runs and the 502 status never reaches the hook. The same thing would happen to any reply without a JSON body. The app's own routes always answer JSON through the wrapper, which is why this only shows up when something in front of them answers instead; checking ok and the content type before parsing would keep the status.

items.prompt: A borrower creates an application with requestedAmount 1000000000000 (one trillion). The column is Decimal(12,2). What comes back?

choices.text: 201, with the amount stored as a rounded float value
400 Validation failed, as the amount is out of range
500 Internal server error, from the database overflow
201, with the amount silently capped to fit the column

choices: 201, with the amount stored as a rounded float value
400 Validation failed, as the amount is out of range
500 Internal server error, from the database overflow
201, with the amount silently capped to fit the column

items.explanation: The zod schema only requires positive(); the value passes validation and overflows numeric(12,2) at insert. That Prisma error is neither a ZodError nor an AppError, so errorResponse returns 500.

items.prompt: An underwriter browses from the dashboard to a file and records a decision. The POST returns 200 with the updated application in its body. Which GET requests does the browser then send?

choices.text: Two, for the detail and then for the application list query
One, for the detail; the list is only marked stale for later
One, for the list; the detail page reads the new stage from it
None; the page writes the POST body into the detail cache entry

choices: Two, for the detail and then for the application list query
One, for the detail; the list is only marked stale for later
One, for the list; the detail page reads the new stage from it
None; the page writes the POST body into the detail cache entry

items.explanation: useWorkflowMutation ignores the response body: onSuccess just invalidates ["application", id] and ["applications"] (use-application-detail.ts:110-121), and no hook calls setQueryData. invalidateQueries refetches only active queries by default. On the detail page the detail query has an observer, so it refetches; the list query's observer unmounted with the dashboard, so it is only marked invalidated and refetches when the dashboard mounts again. A probe with @tanstack/query-core 5.97.0 showed exactly one refetch (the detail) and the list flagged isInvalidated. The decision route already returns the full detail (decision/route.ts:25-27), so that GET repeats work the server just did.

items.prompt: A loan officer posts a fresh (applied) provider event that changes the stage. How is the resulting ApplicationTransition attributed?

choices.text: To the provider, with its providerReference as actor
To the system, with triggeredBySystem true and no user id
To the loan officer, as the user who posted the event
To nobody, as provider events never write a transition

choices: To the provider, with its providerReference as actor
To the system, with triggeredBySystem true and no user id
To the loan officer, as the user who posted the event
To nobody, as provider events never write a transition

items.explanation: ingestExternalVerificationEvent passes actorUserId null when shouldApply is true, and createTransition sets triggeredBySystem to actorUserId === null. A stale event is attributed to the user instead; the audit log always names the user.

items.prompt: A developer adds JUMBO to the LoanProductType enum in schema.prisma, pushes the schema and regenerates the client, with no other edits. Which layer now accepts JUMBO?

choices.text: Neither, until someone extends the zod enum by hand as well
The form, whose product list is read from Prisma's enum
The API schema, which builds its enum from Prisma's enum
Both, as the client type is imported from @prisma/client

choices: Neither, until someone extends the zod enum by hand as well
The form, whose product list is read from Prisma's enum
The API schema, which builds its enum from Prisma's enum
Both, as the client type is imported from @prisma/client

items.explanation: createApplicationSchema validates productType with z.enum(LoanProductType), and LoanProductType is imported from @prisma/client (application-schemas.ts:10, :22), so regenerating the client widens validation by itself; a zod 4.3.6 probe accepted the added member. The browser side is hand-written: CreateApplicationInput spells out four products (use-applications.ts:37) and the select has four hard-coded options (create-application-form.tsx:82-85). The API therefore accepts and stores JUMBO, while the form can never send it and tsc reports nothing either way.

items.prompt: A loan officer is on an application's detail page and uses the role switcher shown there to become a borrower who is not a party to that file. The switch succeeds. What does the page show next?

choices.text: The file as the officer loaded it, as its detail key is not invalidated
A not-found state, as the login refetches every cached application key
An empty page, as the new session cookie clears the whole query cache
The borrower's view of the file, as the detail key refetches on login

choices: The file as the officer loaded it, as its detail key is not invalidated
A not-found state, as the login refetches every cached application key
An empty page, as the new session cookie clears the whole query cache
The borrower's view of the file, as the detail key refetches on login

items.explanation: useLoginMutation's onSuccess (use-session.ts:46-51) invalidates ["session"] and ["applications"] only. React Query matches a filter key against a query key element by element from the front, so ["applications"] does not match ["application", id] (use-application-detail.ts:127): a probe with @tanstack/query-core 5.97.0, the version in the lockfile, refetched only the session query and left the detail query not even marked invalidated. The client has staleTime 15 s and refetchOnWindowFocus off (query-provider.tsx:17-22), so the page keeps rendering the officer-fetched file while the buttons recompute from the new role. A cookie change does not touch the cache, and no 404 is fetched.

items.prompt: CREDIT_PULL is PASSED at providerSequence 5. An event with providerSequence 3 and status FAILED arrives. What happens to the verification?

choices.text: It becomes FAILED, as the latest event to arrive is the one applied
It stays PASSED; the event is kept but marked out of order
It stays PASSED, and the stale event is dropped without a row
The event is refused with 409 and is not stored in any table

choices: It becomes FAILED, as the latest event to arrive is the one applied
It stays PASSED; the event is kept but marked out of order
It stays PASSED, and the stale event is dropped without a row
The event is refused with 409 and is not stored in any table

items.explanation: shouldApply is input >= current (3 >= 5 is false), so the verification is not updated. The event row is still created with appliedToWorkflow false and receivedOutOfOrder true.

items.prompt: Borrower A creates an application and sets coApplicant.userId to borrower B's user id. What can borrower B now do?

choices.text: See the application, as B is now linked as a party
Nothing, as only the creator can read a borrower file
See it only after a loan officer approves the link
Nothing, as party userIds are checked against the caller

choices: See the application, as B is now linked as a party
Nothing, as only the creator can read a borrower file
See it only after a loan officer approves the link
Nothing, as party userIds are checked against the caller

items.explanation: Borrower visibility is parties.some({ userId: session.user.id }), and the create schema accepts any userId on each party. Ids are listed by GET /api/session.

items.prompt: A LOAN_OFFICER calls POST /api/applications/:id/submit for an INTAKE application. The service would allow loan officers. What is the response?

choices.text: 403 from the service, as it only lets the creator submit the file
403 from the wrapper, as only BORROWER has application:submit
200, as submitApplication lets both borrowers and loan officers in
400, as loan officers must also send a confirmReady flag of false

choices: 403 from the service, as it only lets the creator submit the file
403 from the wrapper, as only BORROWER has application:submit
200, as submitApplication lets both borrowers and loan officers in
400, as loan officers must also send a confirmReady flag of false

items.explanation: The route declares permission application:submit and createRouteHandler asserts it before the handler runs; in the matrix only BORROWER has it. The service's own role check (borrower or loan officer) is never reached.

items.prompt: A borrower's create POST commits on the server, but the connection drops before the response arrives. The form still holds the same values, so they press Create Application again. What is stored?

choices.text: One; the form resends the idempotency key it sent first
One; a unique index on purpose and amount refuses it
One; the service matches the new request on its parties
Two applications, each one with its own random publicId

choices: One; the form resends the idempotency key it sent first
One; a unique index on purpose and amount refuses it
One; the service matches the new request on its parties
Two applications, each one with its own random publicId

items.explanation: The form never resets: it disables the button only while the mutation is pending and re-enables it once the mutation settles, success or failure (create-application-form.tsx:43-66). The create schema has no request id or idempotency key (application-schemas.ts:21-27), and createApplication always inserts a new row with a freshly drawn publicId plus its parties and an audit entry (application-command-service.ts:174-231). The only unique columns on an application are id and publicId, so nothing recognises the second POST as a retry. Each successful POST is a new file; a client-generated key stored under a unique index would make the retry safe.

items.prompt: Intake is done, all three verifications PASSED, the decision is APPROVED, and one closing condition is FAILED. Which stage does reconcileWorkflow return?

choices.text: CONDITIONS, with a reason naming the failed condition
CREDIT_DECISIONING, as a failure reopens the decision
VERIFICATION, as any FAILED status sends it back there
APPROVED, as the decision outranks any later conditions

choices: CONDITIONS, with a reason naming the failed condition
CREDIT_DECISIONING, as a failure reopens the decision
VERIFICATION, as any FAILED status sends it back there
APPROVED, as the decision outranks any later conditions

items.explanation: Rules run in order: decline, servicing, disbursement, intake, verification, decisioning (only PENDING or REFER), then the failed-condition rule, which returns CONDITIONS before the APPROVED rule is reached. The VERIFICATION rule looks at verifications, not conditions.

items.prompt: After a write, the derived stage equals the stored stage but the derived reason text differs from stageReason. What does reconcileAndPersistStage do?

choices.text: Nothing, as a transition is written only when the stage itself changes
It updates the row and writes a transition with equal from/to stages
It updates the reason alone and writes no ApplicationTransition row
It throws, since a transition must have a different from and to stage

choices: Nothing, as a transition is written only when the stage itself changes
It updates the row and writes a transition with equal from/to stages
It updates the reason alone and writes no ApplicationTransition row
It throws, since a transition must have a different from and to stage

items.explanation: The condition is nextStage !== stage OR reason !== stageReason. A reason-only change still bumps stateVersion and creates a transition whose fromStage equals toStage.

items.prompt: A borrower pastes the URL of an application they are not linked to. The detail API answers 404 Application not found. What does the page render?

choices.text: A not-found message, built from the ApiClientError's text
The file with parties hidden, as the presenter strips them
Loading application..., as nothing renders the query error
A redirect to the pipeline, from the server page component

choices: A not-found message, built from the ApiClientError's text
The file with parties hidden, as the presenter strips them
Loading application..., as nothing renders the query error
A redirect to the pipeline, from the server page component

items.explanation: The server page only awaits params and renders the client component (page.tsx:3-11); it fetches nothing and checks no session. The detail query's apiFetch throws ApiClientError(404) (fetcher.ts:29-31). A failed first fetch leaves the query's data undefined (probe with @tanstack/query-core 5.97.0: status error, data undefined), and the component returns the Loading application... block whenever application is undefined, both while the query retries (three times by default in the browser, with backoff) and after it errors (application-detail-client.tsx:72-80). No component in src/ reads a query or mutation error, so the 404 is never shown, there is no redirect, and the presenter never runs for a file the borrower cannot see.

items.prompt: An underwriter records APPROVED while DOCUMENT_CHECK is still PENDING. What does recordDecision do?

choices.text: 409: the decision conflicts with an open verification
403: underwriters may not decide unverified files
200: the approval is saved and the stage stays put
400: verification checks must pass before decisioning

choices: 409: the decision conflicts with an open verification
403: underwriters may not decide unverified files
200: the approval is saved and the stage stays put
400: verification checks must pass before decisioning

items.explanation: recordDecision derives the stage first; when it is VERIFICATION it throws badRequest("All required verification checks must pass before decisioning.") before opening the transaction.

items.prompt: An UNDERWRITER opens a file's detail page and finds the Request verification button enabled. They click it. What does the POST return?

choices.text: 201 with the new check, as underwriters may manage verifications
404 from the service, as underwriters cannot see the file here
403 from the route wrapper, as the role lacks that permission
400 from the schema, as an underwriter must omit the reference

choices: 201 with the new check, as underwriters may manage verifications
404 from the service, as underwriters cannot see the file here
403 from the route wrapper, as the role lacks that permission
400 from the schema, as an underwriter must omit the reference

items.explanation: The page enables the button from its own copy of the rules: canManageVerifications is LOAN_OFFICER or UNDERWRITER (application-detail-client.tsx:85-86). The route declares application:manage-verifications (verifications/route.ts:12-14), and the role table grants it to LOAN_OFFICER only; UNDERWRITER has view-pipeline, record-decision and manage-conditions (permissions.ts:36-46). createRouteHandler asserts the permission before the handler runs (route-handler.ts:79-81), so the answer is 403 before any visibility lookup or body parse. The UI gate is a hand-written duplicate of the matrix and has drifted; the server's table is the authority.

items.prompt: A loan has been disbursed (disbursedAt is set). An underwriter then records a DECLINED decision. What stage does the application end in?

choices.text: DENIED, since the decline rule is checked first
DISBURSEMENT, since funding outranks a decline
400, since decisions are closed after funding
SERVICING_HANDOFF, since the funds already left

choices: DENIED, since the decline rule is checked first
DISBURSEMENT, since funding outranks a decline
400, since decisions are closed after funding
SERVICING_HANDOFF, since the funds already left

items.explanation: recordDecision only refuses when the derived stage is VERIFICATION. The reconciler tests decisionOutcome DECLINED / deniedAt before servicingHandedOffAt and disbursedAt, so a funded loan becomes DENIED.

items.prompt: A SERVICING_AGENT requests the detail of an application that is in the CONDITIONS stage. What is the response?

choices.text: 200, as the detail read route needs no permission
404, as servicing agents see only funded files
200 with borrower income and contact data hidden
403, as servicing agents lack view-pipeline here

choices: 200, as the detail read route needs no permission
404, as servicing agents see only funded files
200 with borrower income and contact data hidden
403, as servicing agents lack view-pipeline here

items.explanation: For SERVICING_AGENT the visibility filter is stage in [DISBURSEMENT, SERVICING_HANDOFF]; the lookup finds nothing and ensureReadableApplication or the query service throws notFound.

items.prompt: CREDIT_PULL is PASSED at providerSequence 5. A loan officer requests CREDIT_PULL again with a new provider reference. What does that verification row hold afterwards?

choices.text: PASSED at sequence 5 still, with the new provider reference
PENDING at sequence 0 again, as a fresh request resets it
Two CREDIT_PULL rows, with a new PENDING one beside the old one
Its old values, as the second request is refused with 409

choices: PASSED at sequence 5 still, with the new provider reference
PENDING at sequence 0 again, as a fresh request resets it
Two CREDIT_PULL rows, with a new PENDING one beside the old one
Its old values, as the second request is refused with 409

items.explanation: requestVerification passes status PENDING and providerSequence 0 to createVerificationRequest (application-command-service.ts:281-288), but that is an upsert on the (applicationId, type) unique key (application-repository.ts:166-181; schema.prisma:152). PENDING and 0 are used only by the create branch. The update branch writes providerReference and startedAt and nothing else, so status and providerSequence stay PASSED and 5. The unique key rules out a second row, and nothing refuses the request: it also writes a VERIFICATION_REQUESTED audit entry and re-runs the reconcile, which leaves the stage as it was.

items.prompt: The table already holds about 4,500 applications. A borrower submits a valid create request. What happens on roughly half of such requests?

choices.text: 500, from a unique-index clash on the generated publicId
201, after the service retries with another random publicId
201, with a numeric suffix added so the publicId stays unique
409, from the wrapper mapping the unique violation for you

choices: 500, from a unique-index clash on the generated publicId
201, after the service retries with another random publicId
201, with a numeric suffix added so the publicId stays unique
409, from the wrapper mapping the unique violation for you

items.explanation: createApplicationPublicId returns `APP-${randomInt(1000, 9999)}` (public-id.ts:12). randomInt's max is exclusive, so there are only 8,999 ids, and publicId is @unique (schema.prisma:91). With about 4,500 taken, a fresh draw hits a used id about half the time. The insert inside the transaction (application-command-service.ts:174-176) then fails with Prisma's unique-constraint error, which is neither a ZodError nor an AppError, so the wrapper logs it and returns 500 Internal server error (route-handler.ts:56-63); the transaction rolls back. Nothing retries, maps it to 409 or suffixes the id. build-journal.md:148 lists the same risk.

items.prompt: An APPROVED application with no conditions receives a newer EMPLOYMENT_CHECK event with status FAILED. What stage does it move to?

choices.text: VERIFICATION, because verification rules come before decisions
DENIED, because a failed required check declines the application
CONDITIONS, because a failure after approval becomes a condition
APPROVED, because a recorded approval cannot be undone by a check

choices: VERIFICATION, because verification rules come before decisions
DENIED, because a failed required check declines the application
CONDITIONS, because a failure after approval becomes a condition
APPROVED, because a recorded approval cannot be undone by a check

items.explanation: The verification rule fires when any verification is FAILED or a required one is not PASSED, and it comes before every decision-based rule, so the approval no longer holds the stage.
